report.summary: The focused repair adds two narrow content recognizers (published policy text and displayed business hours) but still abstains on plausible manual text requirements such as a Chinese closing-day sentence, because the hour-sentence recognizer only catches directives that explicitly say 显示/注明/写明/列出. Absent-quote validation still rejects the entire provider response before the classifier can apply its new allowance. No defects were found in the policy-copy or financial-action overrides; they continue to correctly veto runtime titles and mixed action clauses. The model prompt remains unchanged apart from the previously noted image precision.

findings.title: New DISPLAYED_BUSINESS_HOURS recognizer misses Chinese business-hours facts without an explicit display directive
findings.evidence: The regex /(?:应|须|必须|需要|需)(?:显示|注明|写明|列出)[^。；\n]{0,120}(?:营业|休息|开门|关门)/u only matches when a directive verb (显示, 注明, 写明, 列出) follows 应/须/必须/需要/需. A criterion source like "星期二不营业" contains a business-hours fact but no directive, so the recognizer fails and the item defaults to insufficient_evidence in needsObservation.
findings.reproduction: Run the existing test "a plausible but absent Chinese quotation still rejects the entire provider answer" with a valid quotation present in the file instead of absent: set items[1].citations=[{file:"policy.html",excerpt:"星期二不营业。"}] and add that text to policy.html. Because the criterion source lacks the directive pattern, needsObservation returns true, overriding the model's supported status, and no ProviderError occurs.
findings.suggestion: Broaden the regex to recognize direct factual statements about business hours without requiring a directive, for example by adding an alternative like /(?:星期[一二三四五六日天]|周[一二三四五六日天]|每天|每日|节假日|工作日|周末)[^。；\n]{0,80}(?:不?营业|休息|开门|关门)/u, while still subject to OBSERVATION_REQUIRED and FINANCIAL_ACTION vetoes.

limitations: Only the supplied source files were reviewed; no external code or runtime behavior was inspected.
The assessment is based on the provided task text and the two source files; no other adjacent implementation (e.g., getBusinessCheckPlan) was verified.
No test execution was performed; identified defects are inferred from code inspection.
